newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end near lows, only SanPaolo shines.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end near lows, only SanPaolo shines.

text.p: Italian shares closed just off the day's lows on Monday after a lacklustre session of range-trading in only moderate volume in a market lacking impetus, traders said.
But banking group Istituto San Paolo di Torino closed 3.28 percent higher at 11,825 lire on 1996 results which showed a 36 percent rise in consolidated net profit.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.64 percent down at 12,277 and the Mib30 blue chip index was 0.62 percent off at 18,311.

"It was a directionless market, losing ground despite firmer Btp bond futures," one trader said. The market showed no reaction to upbeat comments by Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on inflation and Italy's public accounts.
Traded volume was estimated at around 640 billion lire against over one trillion lire on Friday.
Apart from San Paolo, banks tended to be easier with Ambroveneto off 3.95 percent at 4,234 lire and Banca Commerciale Italiana down 1.36 percent at 3,687.
Telecoms were easier, with Telecom Italia under pressure closing 2.65 percent down at 4,334 lire.

Energy group ENI posted a modest 0.2 percent rise to 8,926 lire and Fiat gained 0.42 percent to 5,230, but Olivetti, the most traded stock, lost 1.95 percent to 618.7 lire with over 21 million shares changing hands.
